Here we take in the cleaned ArcasHLA genotype data that is formatted for each MHC gene as a binary matrix. The full allele set is used  - including those with low frequency.

```{r}
all_mhc_genotypes <- readRDS( 
  glue("{hla_dir}/MHC_all_cleaned_unfiltered_2025-07-21.rds")
  ) %>% 
  tibble::rownames_to_column(var = "participant_id") %>% 
  glimpse()

```


Using data provided [here](https://github.com/immunogenomics/cdr3-QTL/tree/main/data/hla_4d_to_aa) we will convert the 4 digit HLA allele codes provided by ArcasHLA to Amino acid specific sites.

```{r}
aa_mapping <- list.files(hla_4d_to_aa_dir) %>% 
  discard(grepl("no_", .)) %>% 
  purrr::set_names() %>% 
  purrr::map(~ read.table(glue("{hla_4d_to_aa_dir}/{.x}"), 
    header=T, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)) %>% 
  bind_rows(.id = "input_file") %>% 
  dplyr::select(-input_file) %>% 
  glimpse()

# list of allele positions that need don't have an amino acid mapping in the previous table
no_aa_mapping <- read.table(glue("{hla_4d_to_aa_dir}/no_amino_acid_allele.info"), 
  header=FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(aatype = V1, HLA_AA_site = V2) %>% 
  glimpse()

long_aa_mapped_df <- all_mhc_genotypes %>% 
    tidyr::pivot_longer(!participant_id, names_to = "fdigit", values_to = "allele_dosage") %>% 
    left_join(aa_mapping, relationship = "many-to-many") %>% 
    glimpse()

full_aa_hla_sites <- long_aa_mapped_df %>% 
    left_join(no_aa_mapping, relationship = "many-to-many") %>% # adds no_aa_mapping df
    # filter(grepl("AA_DRB1_13_", aatype)) %>% glimpse()
    mutate(HLA_AA_site = case_when( # pulls AA from aatype if no mapping is found
      is.na(HLA_AA_site) ~ strex::str_after_last(aatype, "_"),
      TRUE ~ HLA_AA_site
    )) %>% 
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(aatype)) %>% # not found in mapping table
    mutate(hla_site = strex::str_after_first(aatype, "_") %>% strex::str_before_nth( "_", 2)) %>% 
    mutate(hla_gene = strex::str_before_first(hla_site, "_")) %>% 
    glimpse()

saveRDS(full_aa_hla_sites, glue("{gdata_dir}/all_hla_AA_sites_{Sys.Date()}.rds"))

```

```{r}
# Define a function to trim after second colon
format_hla_allele <- function(x) {
    # Count the number of colons
    colon_count <- stringr::str_count(x, "\\:")
    #   message(colon_count)f

    if (colon_count > 1) {
        res <- strex::str_before_last(x, ":") %>% gsub("\\:|\\*", "_", .)
        return(res)
    } else {
        res <- gsub("\\:|\\*", "_", x)
        return(res)
    }
}
format_hla_allele_vec <- Vectorize(format_hla_allele)

remove_genotypes_hwe <- c()
remove_genotypes_freq <- c()
genotype_df_list <- list()
mhc_genes <- c("A", "B", "C", "DPA1", "DPB1", "DQA1", "DQB1", "DRB1")
for (gene in mhc_genes) {
    message(glue("Processing {gene}..."))
    gcopies <- paste0(gene, 1:2)

    # Extract and clean allele names
    alleles_df <- gdf %>%
        dplyr::select(participant_id, all_of(gcopies)) %>%
        dplyr::mutate_at(
            vars(contains(gcopies)),
            ~ replace_na(., "") %>% format_hla_allele_vec()
        ) %>%
        dplyr::mutate_at(
            vars(contains(gcopies)),
            ~ paste0("HLA_", .x)
        )

    # Get unique allele names across both columns
    allele1_values <- unique(alleles_df[[gcopies[1]]])
    allele2_values <- unique(alleles_df[[gcopies[2]]])
    all_alleles <- unique(c(allele1_values, allele2_values)) %>% 
      discard(~ . == "HLA_") # remove empty strings

    # Create empty result dataframe
    result_df <- data.frame(participant_id = alleles_df$participant_id)

    # Fill in counts for each allele
    for (allele in all_alleles) {
        result_df[[allele]] <- 0
        # Check allele1
        result_df[[allele]] <- result_df[[allele]] +
            ifelse(alleles_df[[gcopies[1]]] == allele, 1, 0)
        # Check allele2
        result_df[[allele]] <- result_df[[allele]] +
            ifelse(alleles_df[[gcopies[2]]] == allele, 1, 0)
    }

    # Add row sum
    # message("Row sum table:")
    print(table(rowSums(result_df[, -1])))
    
    allele_freqs <- result_df %>%
        dplyr::select(-c(participant_id)) %>%
        colSums()
    # need at least 5 unique donors with the genotype to be included (5*2 for both alleles)
    maf <- 10 / nrow(result_df)
    freq <- allele_freqs / (2 * nrow(result_df))
    remove_genotypes_freq <- c(
        remove_genotypes_freq,
        names(freq)[freq < 0.01], names(freq)[freq > 0.99]
        # names(freq)[freq < maf], names(freq)[freq > 0.99]
    )

    df <- result_df %>%
        column_to_rownames(var = "participant_id") %>%
        as.matrix()

    hwe_p <- apply(df, 2, function(x) {
        x <- as.numeric(x)
        # observed data
        a0 <- length(x[x == 0])
        a1 <- length(x[x == 1])
        a2 <- length(x[x == 2])

        freq <- sum(x) / (2 * length(x))
        # expedted data
        P_a0 <- (1 - freq)^2
        P_a1 <- 2 * (1 - freq) * freq
        P_a2 <- freq^2

        chitest <- chisq.test(c(a0, a1, a2), p = c(P_a0, P_a1, P_a2)) # simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 2000
        chitest$p.value
    })

    remove_genotypes_hwe <- c(remove_genotypes_hwe, 
      names(hwe_p[hwe_p <= 1e-04])
    )
    
    genotype_df_list[[gene]] <- result_df %>%
        column_to_rownames(var = "participant_id") %>% 
        dplyr::select(-any_of(
          c(remove_genotypes_freq, remove_genotypes_hwe)
          )) %>% 
        glimpse()
    
}

message(glue(
    "\n\nFLAG: Low/high frequency genotypes: \n",
    "{paste(remove_genotypes_freq, collapse = ', ')}"
))

message(glue(
    "\n\nFLAG: Hardy-Weinberg Non-independence:\n",
    " {paste(remove_genotypes_hwe, collapse = ', ')}"
))

```


Performing PCA on genotype data

```{r}
mhc1_alleles <- c("A", "B", "C")
mhc2_alleles <- c("DPA1", "DPB1", "DQA1", "DQB1", "DRB1")

# Aggregate genotypes into class I and class II
mhc1_genotypes <- mhc1_alleles %>% 
  purrr::map(~ genotype_df_list[[.x]]) %>% 
  bind_cols() %>% 
  glimpse()
mhc2_genotypes <- mhc2_alleles %>% 
  purrr::map(~ genotype_df_list[[.x]]) %>% 
  bind_cols() %>% 
  glimpse()
all_mhc_genotypes <- bind_cols(mhc1_genotypes, mhc2_genotypes) %>% glimpse()

#PCA
pca_mhc1 <- prcomp(as.matrix(mhc1_genotypes), scale = TRUE)
pca_mhc1_df <- pca_mhc1$x %>% as.data.frame()
pca_mhc2 <- prcomp(as.matrix(mhc2_genotypes), scale = TRUE)
pca_mhc2_df <- pca_mhc2$x %>% as.data.frame()
pca_mhc_all <- prcomp(as.matrix(all_mhc_genotypes), scale = TRUE)
pca_mhc_all_df <- pca_mhc_all$x %>% as.data.frame()

collect_cumvar <- function(pca_obj, df_tag) {
  data.frame("cumprop" = summary(pca_obj)$importance["Cumulative Proportion", ]) %>% 
    tibble::rownames_to_column(var = "PC") %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(PC_num = PC %>% gsub("PC", "", .) %>% as.numeric()) %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(MHC = df_tag)
}

mhc1_cumvar <- collect_cumvar(pca_mhc1, "MHCI")
mhc2_cumvar <- collect_cumvar(pca_mhc2, "MHCII")
mhc_all_cumvar <- collect_cumvar(pca_mhc_all, "MHC_all")

# how many PCs are needed to explain at least 80% of the variance?
list(mhc1_cumvar, mhc2_cumvar, mhc_all_cumvar) %>% purrr::map(
  ~ {{filter(., cumprop >= 0.8) %>% slice_min(PC_num) %>% pull(PC)}}
)

p_mhc_cumulative_variance <- bind_rows(mhc1_cumvar,mhc2_cumvar, mhc_all_cumvar) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = PC_num, y = cumprop, color = MHC)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = MHC), size = 1.5) +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_color_d3() +
  labs(x = "Principal Component Dimension", y = "Cumulative Proportion of Variance")

ggsave(
  glue("{hla_plots_dir}/PCA/mhc_pca_cumulative_variance.png"),
  plot = p_mhc_cumulative_variance,
  width = 10,
  height = 6
)

# Saving filtered Genotype data
hla_dir <- glue("{wkdir}/data/interim/airr/arcasHLA/analysis_cleaned")
pca_dir <- glue("{hla_dir}/pca_data")

saveRDS(all_mhc_genotypes, 
  glue("{hla_dir}/MHC_all_cleaned_{Sys.Date()}.rds")
)
saveRDS(mhc1_genotypes, 
  glue("{hla_dir}/MHCI_cleaned_{Sys.Date()}.rds")
)
saveRDS(mhc2_genotypes, 
  glue("{hla_dir}/MHCII_cleaned_{Sys.Date()}.rds")
)

# Save MHC PCA metadata
saveRDS(pca_mhc1, glue("{pca_dir}/pca_MHCI_{Sys.Date()}.rds"))
saveRDS(pca_mhc2, glue("{pca_dir}/pca_MHCII_{Sys.Date()}.rds"))
saveRDS(pca_mhc_all, glue("{pca_dir}/pca_MHC_all_{Sys.Date()}.rds"))

pca_mhc1_final_df <- pca_mhc1_df %>% 
  dplyr::rename_all(~paste0("MHC_I_", .))
pca_mhc2_final_df <- pca_mhc2_df %>% 
  dplyr::rename_all(~paste0("MHC_II_", .))
pca_mhc_all_final_df <- pca_mhc_all_df %>% 
  dplyr::rename_all(~paste0("MHC_all_", .))
pca_mhc_combined_final_df <- bind_cols(
  pca_mhc1_final[, 1:10],
  pca_mhc2_final[, 1:10],
  pca_mhc_all_final[, 1:10],
) %>% glimpse()

saveRDS(pca_mhc1_final_df, glue("{pca_dir}/df_pca_MHCI_{Sys.Date()}.rds"))
saveRDS(pca_mhc2_df, glue("{pca_dir}/df_pca_MHCII_{Sys.Date()}.rds"))
saveRDS(pca_mhc_all_df, glue("{pca_dir}/df_pca_MHC_all_{Sys.Date()}.rds"))
saveRDS(pca_mhc_combined_final_df, glue("{pca_dir}/df_pca_MHC_all_{Sys.Date()}.rds"))

```



![Cumulative Explained Variance by MHC Class](../figures/AIRR/arcasHLA/PCA/mhc_pca_cumulative_variance.png)

**Key Takeaway**

- MHC I and II have similar cumulative explained variance with 80% variance explained by 29 and 24 components, respectively.

- The combined binary matrix requires 49 PCs to explain 80% of the variance. 

- Each of the first few PCs explain only a small portion of the variance. (3-5%)


```{r}
pid_meta <- full_meta_df %>%
    select(participant_id, case_control_other_latest, ethnicity, race, sex, study) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    glimpse()

plot_mhc_pca <- function(pca_obj, colorvar, pca_dim1, pca_dim2) {
    pca_df <- pca_obj$x %>% as.data.frame()
    var_explained <- pca_obj$sdev^2 / sum(pca_obj$sdev^2)
    percent_var <- round(100 * var_explained, 1)

    pca_df %>%
        rownames_to_column(var = "participant_id") %>%
        left_join(pid_meta, by = "participant_id") %>%
        drop_na({{ colorvar }}) %>%
        dplyr::slice_sample(prop = 1) %>%
        ggplot(aes(x = {{ pca_dim1 }}, y = {{ pca_dim2 }}, color = .data[[colorvar]])) +
        stat_ellipse(type = "norm", level = 0.95) +
        geom_point() +
        scale_color_d3() +
        coord_fixed() +
        theme_bw() +
        labs(
            x = paste0("PC1 (", percent_var[1], "%)"),
            y = paste0("PC2 (", percent_var[2], "%)")
        )
}

# # sample execution
# plot_mhc_pca(pca_mhc1, ethnicity, PC1, PC2)
pca_obj_list <- list(pca_mhc1, pca_mhc2, pca_mhc_all)
names(pca_obj_list) <- c("mhc1", "mhc2", "mhc_all")

for (i in seq_along(pca_obj_list)) {
  pca_obj <- pca_obj_list[[i]]
  pca_obj_name <- names(pca_obj_list)[i]

  for (var in c("ethnicity", "race", "study", "case_control_other_latest")) {
    p <- plot_mhc_pca(pca_obj, var, PC1, PC2)
    ggsave(glue("{hla_plots_dir}/PCA/{pca_obj_name}_pca_{var}.png"), plot = p, width = 10, height = 10)
  }
}

```

![PCA of MHC II](../figures/AIRR/arcasHLA/PCA/mhc2_pca_case_control_other_latest.png)


**Key Takeaways**

- MHC I distributions seem more normal while MHC II distributions seem more structured with subclusters
- There appears to be no distinct subclusters of samples by case/control status nor ethnicity, sex, or race.


## EVERYTHING before this is now redunant with HLA-Analysis.qmd




```{r}
library(midasHLA)

dat_pheno <-
  read.table(
  file = system.file("extdata", "MiDAS_tut_pheno.txt", package = "midasHLA"),
  header = TRUE
  )
dat_HLA <-
  readHlaCalls(
  file = system.file("extdata", "MiDAS_tut_HLA.txt", package = "midasHLA"),
  resolution = 4
  )

dat_pheno %>% View()
dat_HLA %>% View()

freq_HLA <- getHlaFrequencies(hla_calls = dat_HLA, compare = TRUE) %>%
  filter(Freq > 0.01)

freq_HLA_long <- tidyr::gather(
  data = freq_HLA,
  key = "population",
  value = "freq",
  "Freq",
  "USA NMDP European Caucasian",
  "USA NMDP Chinese",
  "USA NMDP African American pop 2",
  factor_key = TRUE
) %>% 
  filter(grepl("^A", allele))

plot_HLAfreq <-
  ggplot2::ggplot(data = freq_HLA_long, ggplot2::aes(x = allele, y = freq, fill = population)) +
  ggplot2::geom_bar(
    stat = "identity",
    position = ggplot2::position_dodge(0.7),
    width = 0.7,
    colour = "black"
  ) +
  ggplot2::coord_flip() +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(labels = formattable::percent)

plot_HLAfreq
```


# Are classical HLA alleles more common in PD?
```{r}
HLA <- prepareMiDAS(
  hla_calls = dat_HLA,
  colData = dat_pheno,
  experiment = "hla_alleles"
)

nrow(freq_HLA)

HLA <- HWETest(
  object = HLA,
  experiment = "hla_alleles",
  HWE_cutoff = 0.05 / 447,
  as.MiDAS = TRUE
)

```


```{r}
HLA_model <- glm(disease ~ term, data = HLA, family = binomial())
HLA_results <- runMiDAS(
  object = HLA_model, 
  experiment = "hla_alleles", 
  inheritance_model = "dominant",
  lower_frequency_cutoff = 0.02, 
  upper_frequency_cutoff = 0.98, 
  correction = "bonferroni", 
  exponentiate = TRUE
)

kableResults(HLA_results)

HLA_results_cond <- runMiDAS(
  object = HLA_model, 
  experiment = "hla_alleles", 
  inheritance_model = "dominant", 
  conditional = TRUE,
  lower_frequency_cutoff = 0.02, 
  upper_frequency_cutoff = 0.98, 
  correction = "bonferroni", 
  exponentiate = TRUE
)

kableResults(HLA_results_cond)
```
